You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented

# Outcome sub-dossier — Albany Molecular Research, Inc. (later "Curia") realized record after go-private, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; the traceable realized record is
> limited to the deregistration filing and reputable press. This sub-dossier contains no

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On August 31, 2017 — the same date the merger closed — Albany Molecular Research, Inc.
  filed a Form 15 (accession-tagged "15-12B") certifying termination of registration of
  its common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act (and/or suspension of its
  reporting duty under Sections 13(a)/15(d)); the filing recorded approximately one (1)
  holder of record as of the certification date, and listed "None" for any other class of
  securities for which a duty to file reports remained. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-17-046133, Form 15-12B]
- The Form 15 was signed by William S. Marth in his capacity as President and Chief
  Executive Officer. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-17-046133, Form 15-12B]
- A search of Albany Molecular Research, Inc.'s (CIK 0001065087) EDGAR filing history
  finds no Form 10-K, Form 10-Q, Form 8-K, or Form 20-F filed after August 31, 2017; no
  periodic report covering any fiscal year within the ~2020-2022 outcome window was
  located under this CIK. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001065087&type=10-K]
- Numerous unaffiliated closed-end credit funds and CLO-type vehicles (e.g., Blackstone/
  GSO- and Eaton Vance-managed funds, KKR Credit Opportunities Portfolio, BlackRock
  Floating Rate Income Trust) filed their own SEC Form NPORT-P portfolio-holdings reports
  during 2019-2021 listing "Albany Molecular Research" as a floating-rate loan holding,
  indicating the company's post-merger term debt continued to be held and traded in the
  institutional loan market; these are third-party holders' own disclosures, not a
  filing by AMRI/Curia itself, and do not include AMRI/Curia's own financial statements.
  [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=albany+molecular&type=NPORT-P&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]

## Realized business record under private ownership (press-sourced)
- Effective July 12, 2021, the company changed its name from Albany Molecular Research,
  Inc. ("AMRI") to Curia, introducing a new brand identity and website; at that time the
  company was reported to employ "more than 3,000 people in 21 locations around the
  world," including more than 600 chemists, 70 biologists, 225 senior scientists, and
  approximately 400 quality and regulatory specialists, with 564 active patents. [SRC: https://www.contractpharma.com/breaking-news/amri-becomes-curia/]
- The company's chairman and CEO at the time of the rename was John Ratliff, who
  described the new name as reflecting "the assembled deep expertise of our people, the
  breadth of our products, services and solutions." [SRC: https://www.contractpharma.com/breaking-news/amri-becomes-curia/]
- In March 2021 the company (still named AMRI) was reported to have approximately 3,100
  employees and to have been named to a Forbes list of best employers for 2021,
  notwithstanding "the profound challenges the world faced with the COVID-19 pandemic."
  [SRC: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210309005021/en/AMRI-Earns-Spot-on-Forbes-America's-Best-Employers-2021-List]
- Concurrent with the rebrand, the company pursued expansion into biologics: it
  announced an agreement in July 2021 to acquire biologics formulation and fill-finish
  company Integrity Bio (expected to close by year-end 2021), and it completed an
  acquisition of LakePharma Inc. in early September 2021; industry press dated February
  2022 reported that Integrity Bio and LakePharma were being brought under the unified
  Curia brand. [SRC: https://xtalks.com/global-cdmo-amri-rebrands-as-curia-and-sets-sights-on-biologics-2838/]

## Items sought but not found / not primary-verifiable
- No SEC filing by AMRI/Curia itself (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, or registration statement) was
  located for the ~2020-2022 window, so no audited revenue, net income/loss, or
  impairment/write-down figure for the acquired business can be sourced to a primary
  filing within this window. [UNVERIFIED]
- Third-party aggregator/company-profile sites report post-2017 revenue and employee-
  count figures for AMRI/Curia, but these are not traceable to an audited primary filing
  and are recorded here as [UNVERIFIED] rather than cited as fact. [UNVERIFIED]
- No reputable-press report of a divestiture, bankruptcy, or comparable distress-type
  outcome scalar for AMRI/Curia was located dated within the ~2020-2022 window; later
  reporting on Curia's capital-structure and Spain-asset-sale activity exists but is
  dated 2025-2026, outside the fixed 3-5-year outcome window fixed at construction, and
  is not cited here as an in-window outcome fact. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Albany Molecular Research, Inc. was taken private and deregistered on August
  31, 2017 (the closing date), there is no public audited outcome record (10-K/10-Q) for
  the ~2020-2022 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-17-046133, Form 15-12B]
- The traceable realized-record facts within the fixed window are press-sourced: the
  company continued operating at a comparable-or-larger scale (3,000+ employees in 21
  locations as of mid-2021, versus roughly 3,100 employees reported in March 2021),
  underwent a corporate rebrand from AMRI to Curia (July 2021), and pursued at least two
  acquisitions expanding into biologics manufacturing (Integrity Bio, announced July
  2021; LakePharma, completed September 2021), which were integrated under the Curia
  brand by February 2022. [SRC: https://www.contractpharma.com/breaking-news/amri-becomes-curia/] [SRC: https://xtalks.com/global-cdmo-amri-rebrands-as-curia-and-sets-sights-on-biologics-2838/]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on any financial-scalar
  outcome (revenue, net income, impairment) for the window: the absence of a public
  periodic-reporting record precludes a primary-sourced determination of the realized
  3-5-year financial trajectory of the acquired business, even though non-financial
  press indicators (continued operation, headcount, rebrand, acquisitions) are
  documented within the window.

[SLICE END]
